cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Choose Me
cards.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to my birthday instead. I've cleared a proper dance floor; you can't turn safely between concert seats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already bought tickets. My friend wants dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring her here. Dancing needs space for feet, not just a speaker. I'll set two extra places.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll come straight from work in high heels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend her flat shoes and check the fit. Shall I count you both in before I have to explain the difference between a dance floor and an aisle again?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 corrects concert seating as dance space, A3 distinguishes music from suitable floor and A5 specifies shoes and fit while pressing for A birthday choice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 friend dancing requirement causes A3 including friend on the prepared floor; B4 heels cause A5 loan and fitting before asking both to commit.

relationship.evidence: B2 paid tickets and friend preference remain real rival commitments; B4 adds a practical clothing constraint.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes professional preparation a stronger reason to choose A after B4 reveals another barrier.

specificity.evidence: A1 birthday versus concert and A3 extra places make the invitation intelligible; B4 work shoes explains the new correction.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 final impatience returns to an actual distinction already made rather than an invented friendship catastrophe.
